newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss Nat'l Bank mulled melting Nazi gold - report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Nat'l Bank mulled melting Nazi gold - report.

text.p: Wartime directors of Switzerland's central bank mulled remelting gold purchased from Nazi Germany to hide any traces of its dubious origins, but finally dropped the plan, according to a report published on Wednesday.

Swiss historian Michel Fior found documents in Swiss National Bank (SNB) archives showing two of three bank directors backed the proposal in 1942 for fear the SNB would be unable to re-sell gold reported looted, a Geneva newspaper reported.
But the directors never acted on the plan because other central banks who bought the gold from Switzerland did not raise any complaints, the Journal de Geneve daily said.
Fior could not be reached for comment, but an SNB spokesman spokesman confirmed the report.
"The discussion took place, but in the end no remelting took place," he said, calling Fior's study "a serious and interesting scientific contribution to the historical review of the period".

The paper cited SNB director Paul Rossy's concern that the central banks of Belgium and the Netherlands could still have lists of numbered gold bars that the Nazis looted when they invaded those countries.

"The result would be that these bars could not be resold. Although the risk of damage to the (Swiss) National Bank would not be big, melting (the bars) would exclude all danger," Rossy was quoted as saying.
The Nazis looted millions of dollars worth of gold from the countries they occupied and used it to pay for crucial supplies bought in neutral countries like Switzerland.

The SNB acknowledged in 1985 that it bought 1.2 billion Swiss francs (about $300 million at 1946 exchange rates) worth of gold from Nazi Germany between 1939 and 1945. It agreed in 1946 to pay the Allies 250 million Swiss francs in compensation for the purchases.
The SNB has said any further compensation would have to await the findings of an international panel of historians now reviewing Switzerland's wartime role as a financial centre.
